new_upstream_defects: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:200-201 - the sort classifier tests `$0.hasPrefix("-o")`, which a double-dashed long option can never satisfy. `sort --output=victim.txt in.txt` is therefore classified as a READER. Worst outcome: in Command Code's .auto permission mode the command is auto-approved without the user seeing it (CommandCodeSession.swift:710), and ThreadRuntime.swift:3232 takes no checkpoint for it, so the overwritten file has no base to revert to. Not in upstream_defects.md; no Shell.swift classifier entry exists there at all.

DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:198-199 with :162 - searchActions holds only -delete, -exec, -execdir, -ok, -okdir, -x, -X. `find . -fprintf out.txt '%p\n'` writes a file and is classified as a READER. Same two consequences as the sort case (auto-approval plus no checkpoint). Not in upstream_defects.md.

DroppyCode/Core/Support/Shell.swift:202-204 with :153-159 - gitReaders contains tag, config and remote, so `git config user.email x`, `git tag v1` and `git remote add origin <url>` are classified as READERS. The spec already records this inside PR-TERM-098's failure_cases as upstream behaviour, but the defect register has no entry for it, so it reads as a spec aside rather than a known defect. Worst outcome: a repository-config write is auto-approved in .auto mode and never checkpointed.

DroppyCode/Services/Git/WorkingTreeWatch.swift:191-192 - the cookie rule accepts ANY path under <gitdir>/droppy-code-sync- and raises cookieSeen to its decimal suffix, with no check that this watch wrote it. Any process that can create a file in the git directory (a hook, another tool, a second copy of the app) can release a pending waiter early by naming a large number. Worst outcome: settledGeneration returns while events are still in flight, the capture trusts a stale changed set, and the resulting checkpoint records only part of the tree - which is exactly the harm BLK-0003 is open over, reachable without any cookie timeout. Not in upstream_defects.md.

DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPKeychain.swift:61-67 - deleteAll iterates entry.fields only, so a secret written under a field key the entry no longer declares is never deleted and never enumerated. Worst outcome: a credential the user believes they removed by disconnecting stays in protected storage indefinitely, under an account string nothing in the app will ever look up again. Not in upstream_defects.md (entry 21 covers a different MCPKeychain problem, the missing kSecAttrAccessible on update).

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:715-716 - the gitLabAuth string interpolates {detail} between two hard '\n\n' pairs. When glab's failure message is empty the user reads four consecutive newlines, i.e. a visible gap, in the chat note. Cosmetic only. Not in upstream_defects.md.

consequential_candidates: Shell.swift's read-only classifier is a SECURITY CONTROL, not just a checkpoint optimisation: CommandCodeSession.swift:710 uses ShellCommandKind.mayWriteFiles as the auto-approval gate for shell_command, powershell and monitor_command in .auto permission mode. Faithfully reproducing the three misclassifications above (`sort --output=file`, `find -fprintf file`, `git config`/`git tag`/`git remote add`) means a Windows build auto-runs file-writing and repository-config-writing commands with no user prompt, AND ThreadRuntime.swift:3232 skips the checkpoint for them, so there is nothing to revert. Weakened security control plus silent loss. I specified the behaviour verbatim as parity demands and recorded each misclassification in the new rows' failure_cases, but the decision to reproduce it belongs to the owner and is not covered by any existing BLK entry.

WorkingTreeWatch.swift:191-192 cookie forgery: any writer into the git directory can advance cookieSeen and release a capture's waiter early, producing a checkpoint that silently records only part of the tree. That truncated checkpoint is the precondition BLK-0003 is open over, and a later revert against it deletes untracked, uncommitted work at Git.swift:619 while reporting success. BLK-0003's quarantine is scoped to the cookie-TIMEOUT teardown and to partial captures; this reaches the same harm through a path the entry does not name. Recommend extending BLK-0003's scope or raising a sibling entry before PR-GIT-153 is implemented - I marked PR-GIT-153 SPECIFIED because it is not inside any currently open quarantine, and flag that as the judgement most worth a second look.

MCPKeychain.deleteAll (new PR-MCP-228) destroys credentials with the result discarded, so a locked or unavailable store deletes nothing and disconnect still reports success. Reproduced faithfully, a Windows user who disconnects a server to revoke its key can be told it worked while the key is still in DPAPI/Credential Manager. I recorded it as a failure case and forbade any plaintext fallback in windows_path; whether to keep the silence is a product decision.
